tells.1: Repeated explanatory clauses ('so you…') and flat sentence rhythms make the copy feel mechanically simplified.
tells.2: Stock encouragement such as 'keep you moving forward' and 'look back at how far you've come' feels like generic wellness copy.
tells.3: Stacked reassurance and vague benefits: 'guidance you can trust,' 'always know,' and 'unlock more of what the app has to offer.'
tells.4: The vague Premium benefit, 'adds more to the app,' reads like placeholder copy.

reason: Version 4 has the strongest balance of direct language, useful detail, and restraint, though its Premium benefits need specificity before publication. Version 2 has a more conversational voice but more stock marketing language; these are stylistic judgments, not reliable evidence of AI authorship.
